tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus
Synovial sheath enclosing the extensor digitorum longus tendons in front of the ankle.
tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu: Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longus
Sheath of the big toe extensor tendon in front of the ankle.
tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longu: Tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longus
Sheath of the 3rd extensor compartment, turning around Lister's tubercle.
tendon sheath of extensors carpi radiali: Tendon sheath of extensores carpi radiales
tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis: Tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis
Sheath enclosing the tendon in the groove of the trapezium.
tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus: Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus
Sheath enclosing the tendon in the tarsal tunnel.
tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus: Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus
Sheath enclosing the tendon in the tarsal tunnel.
tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus: Tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus (radial bursa)
Sheath enclosing the thumb flexor tendon from the carpal tunnel to the distal phalanx.
tendon sheath of tibialis anterior: The most medial tendon sheath in front of the ankle.
tendon sheath of tibialis posterior musc: Tendon sheath just behind the medial malleolus.
tensor fasciae latae: Runs from the ASIS to the iliotibial band; flexes and abducts the hip and stabilises knee extension. Superior gluteal nerve.
tenth rib: 10th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.
teres major muscle: Runs from the inferior angle of the scapula to the crest of the lesser tubercle; adducts and medially rotates the arm. Lower subscapular nerve.
teres minor muscle: Rotator cuff muscle from the lateral border of the scapula to the greater tubercle; rotates the arm laterally. Axillary nerve.
third metacarpal bone: The 3rd of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
third metatarsal bone: The 3rd of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
third rib: 3rd rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.
third trochanter: Extra projection seen in some people at the upper end of the gluteal tuberosity; an attachment area for gluteus maximus.
thoracic vertebra: Thoracic vertebra; it carries facets that articulate with the ribs.
thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-arytenoid: Fibres extending to the edge of the epiglottis; they widen the laryngeal inlet.
thyrohyoid muscle: Short muscle from the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid; supplied by C1 fibres (via the hypoglossal nerve), it raises the larynx or depresses the hyoid.
thyroid articular surface: Articular surface on the side of the cricoid; forms the cricothyroid joint with the inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage.
thyroid cartilage: The largest cartilage of the larynx; its two laminae join in front to form the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
tibia: Medial, weight-bearing bone of the leg; its anterior border and medial surface are felt under the skin. Its distal end forms the medial malleolus; it is the long bone most often involved in open fractures.
tibial plateau: Flat upper surface of the tibia; plateau fractures involve the knee joint.
tibial tuberosity: Prominence on the front of the tibia; the patellar ligament inserts here, and Osgood–Schlatter disease occurs here.
tibialis anterior muscle: Runs from the lateral surface of the tibia to the medial cuneiform and 1st metatarsal; lifts the foot (dorsiflexion) and inverts it. Deep fibular nerve; its paralysis causes 'foot drop'.
tibialis posterior muscle: The deepest muscle of the leg; it inserts into the navicular and tarsal bones, inverts the foot and supports the medial arch. Its dysfunction is the commonest cause of acquired flatfoot.
tibiocalcaneal ligament: Part of the deltoid ligament from the medial malleolus to the sustentaculum tali.
tibionavicular ligament: Part of the deltoid ligament from the medial malleolus to the navicular.
transversalis fascia: Fascia lining the inner surface of transversus abdominis; the deep inguinal ring opens in it.
transverse acetabular ligament: Ligament bridging the acetabular notch and completing the labrum; vessels supplying the joint enter beneath it.
transverse arytenoid muscle: The only unpaired muscle, drawing the two arytenoid cartilages together; it closes the posterior part of the glottis.
transverse costal facet: Facet of the transverse process that articulates with the tubercle of the rib.
transverse head of adductor hallucis: Arises from the capsules of the lateral metatarsophalangeal joints; supports the transverse arch.
transverse head of adductor pollicis: Arises from the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal; the muscle adducts the thumb. Ulnar nerve; when weak, Froment's sign is positive.
transverse humeral ligament: Bridges the intertubercular sulcus, holding the tendon of the long head of biceps in place.
transverse intermuscular septum of leg: Fascia dividing the posterior compartment into superficial and deep parts.
transverse ligament of knee: Ligament joining the anterior horns of the two menisci.
transverse ligament tubercle: Tubercle for transverse ligament of atlas
Prominence on the inner surface of the lateral mass; the transverse ligament of the atlas, which holds the dens, attaches here.
transverse part of iliofemoral ligament: Lateral limb of the inverted-Y ligament; limits lateral rotation and extension.
transverse part of trapezius muscle: Middle fibres from the C7–T3 spines to the acromion; retract the scapula.
transverse process: Laterally projecting process of the arch; muscles and ligaments attach to it.
transverse ridges: Transverse lines on the pelvic surface; they mark the boundaries of the fused vertebral bodies.
transverse tibiofibular ligament: Deep part of the posterior tibiofibular ligament; deepens the ankle socket from behind.
transversus abdominis muscle: The deepest flat muscle of the abdominal wall; its fibres are horizontal and, by raising intra-abdominal pressure, it works like a corset. Nerves: T7–L1.
transversus thoracis muscle: Thin muscle from the inner surface of the sternum to the 2nd–6th costal cartilages.
trapeziotrapezoidal interosseous ligamen: Interosseous ligament between the trapezium and trapezoid.
